declared_sampling_rule.replacement_limit: At most one diagnosed infrastructure replacement per arm; retain all attempts. Source, test or measurement-input fixes restart the cohort.
declared_sampling_rule.execution: Sequential complete runs; no artificial project cache or prewarming in either arm
declared_sampling_rule.control: Existing parallel job graph; one instrumented unittest process
declared_sampling_rule.candidate: Identical graph and inputs; two instrumented processes in existing unit-suite job
declared_sampling_rule.assignment: One contiguous split of canonical discovered occurrence order, at the actual-module boundary nearest half the case count, earliest boundary breaks ties
acceptance: All required diagnostic jobs successful with complete reports
Candidate median aggregate job execution below control and all three paired aggregate differences improve
Candidate median elapsed no greater than control
Matching per-phase/platform discovery occurrence multisets and executed case outcomes/skips
Matching native matrix, frozen checkouts, relevant toolchains and dependency versions
declared_sampling_rule.metrics: Elapsed from run creation to last relevant job completion; aggregate sum of job started_at to completed_at, including uniform observer/metadata/artifact overhead; report queue/setup separately
limitations: Job duration measures allocated runner wall time, not CPU time or a billing amount
No line or branch coverage measurement; compare actual unittest execution records and native verification
Hosted image builds, host load and hosted tool-cache warmth may vary; record them and include setup in totals.
declared_sampling_rule.execution_identity_rule: Require identical top-level test IDs, multiplicity and outcomes in each phase/platform; require identical all skip callback IDs/reasons and fixture-suppressed IDs. Retain successful subtest display digests and require matching callback counts. Disclose varying successful parameter displays instead of claiming their textual identities match.
declared_sampling_rule.cohort_restart_reason: Windows lifecycle fixture correction after a native test failed in control-2; the whole interrupted cohort excluded. Both arms use the same on-demand fixture and every original assertion. This is not an infrastructure replacement.
declared_sampling_rule.environment_identity: Require per-role exact Python/platform/CPU/package/compiler and OpenSSL/effective CA certificate-content fingerprints. Record image-build identifiers as observed variation.

infrastructure_replacement.reason: The macOS installer received five logical CPUs rather than the required three; all other strict inputs matched.
infrastructure_replacement.independent_review: Astra requested at max effort; served model and effort unverified
infrastructure_replacement.scope: One complete 15-job run with identical source, harness, labels and inputs
infrastructure_replacement.rule: A failed or ineligible replacement stops this cohort as inconclusive. No further candidate replacement or relaxed predicate.

hash_algorithm: SHA-256 of UTF-8 json.dumps(value, sort_keys=True, separators=(comma, colon)); inventory IDs sorted with duplicates; discovery_order and case_order preserve list order; case/event dictionaries sorted by json.dumps(row, sort_keys=True)
preliminary_exclusion_reason: Different macOS certifi versions could affect a default-CA input; effective CA contents were not recorded. Both attempts passed the same workload but were excluded before a new frozen six-run cohort.
interrupted_cohort_exclusion_reason: An unchanged native Windows lifecycle fixture failed in control-2. Its automatic recovery trigger could race a stopped-state assertion. The whole interrupted cohort was excluded; it was not an infrastructure replacement. Both new arms use the same corrected on-demand fixture, every original assertion, and unchanged production scheduling. Companion native migration and XML contracts retain production triggers.

fixture_proof.method: Real Task Scheduler; 65-second idle window before first legitimate disable; 180-second children in both variants; no synthetic Task.Run

limits: Three successful runs per arm are descriptive, not a reliability guarantee
Runner duration is allocated wall time, not CPU time or a billing amount
No line or branch coverage measurement
Hosted image builds, machine load and tool-cache state are uncontrolled; relevant recorded inputs must match
Aggregate differences include unrelated job and setup variation; they are not a pure causal estimate of worker concurrency
Uniform observer, source/environment capture and artifact costs are included
